claim: The batched 4-qubit QLSTM implementation is computationally feasible on the CPU runtime used in this study.
QLSTM and classical LSTM were compared with near-matched trainable parameter counts (5422 versus 5426).
The classical LSTM validation advantage over the parameter-matched endpoint MLP was reproducible across all five paired random seeds.
QLSTM provides lower validation gain-prediction error than the classical LSTM.
QLSTM outperforms the classical LSTM on the independently held-out test families.
QLSTM outperforms the constant train-mean gain predictor on the held-out test set.
The present QLSTM demonstrates robust gain-estimation generalization across unseen G1/G2 dynamic families.
evidence: Test regime accuracy=0.016875; test/validation MSE ratio=5.441.

claim: QLSTM generalizes to an independently held-out G3 dynamic family.
evidence: G3 has no independent validation/test family in the finalized primary split.

claim: Strong dependence on temporal history/order has been demonstrated for the recurrent baseline.
evidence: Cell 141 showed only weak aggregate sensitivity to sequence-history ablations.

claim: Window-level p-values or statistical significance may be inferred from the 3200 test windows.
evidence: The 3200 overlapping windows represent only two independent held-out dynamic families.

claim: QLSTM may be retrained or retuned after observing the Cell-149 test result.
evidence: Architecture, hyperparameters, and weights were frozen before test evaluation.

claim: Closed-loop evaluation remains necessary because gain-regression error alone does not establish the resulting frequency-control performance.
evidence: Model-stage metrics quantify gain estimation, not closed-loop frequency response.
